_comment: Host-specific review decisions for this machine. Merged on top of the shared recipes/review-overrides.json by bin/extract-*.py: a page here overrides the shared page block-by-block, so shared mechanism decisions survive while the hardware-bound ones live with the host. Nearly every entry names a concrete device, label, GPU driver or /boot path; if a decision is true of any LFS box it belongs in the shared file instead. Exception: ch11-theend, where what differs is this host's book pin, not its hardware -- the shared recipes/ tree has no version scoping, so a stored command embedding a version string has no one correct shared value while server is on 13.1 and laptop on 13.0.

0.cmd:
cat > /etc/fstab << "EOF"
# file system   mount-point    type      options             dump  fsck
#                                                                  order

LABEL=LFSROOT   /              ext4      defaults            1     1
LABEL=LFSSWAP   swap           swap      pri=1               0     0

proc            /proc          proc      nosuid,noexec,nodev 0     0
sysfs           /sys           sysfs     nosuid,noexec,nodev 0     0
devtmpfs        /dev           devtmpfs  mode=0755,nosuid    0     0
devpts          /dev/pts       devpts    gid=5,mode=620      0     0
tmpfs           /run           tmpfs     defaults            0     0
tmpfs           /dev/shm       tmpfs     nosuid,nodev        0     0
cgroup2         /sys/fs/cgroup cgroup2   nosuid,noexec,nodev 0     0
EOF
0.reason: Book's template uses /dev/<xxx> and /dev/<yyy> placeholders. Written with LABEL= so the tree is not bound to a device node that does not exist yet: label the USB root LFSROOT and swap LFSSWAP when creating them. Line order corrected 2026-09-21: the book lists devpts before devtmpfs, which puts the /dev/pts mountpoint ahead of the /dev that contains it -- `findmnt --verify` reports it as a real error ("wrong order: /dev/pts specified before /dev"), the only one it reports on this host. Harmless under systemd, which orders mounts by dependency rather than by file order, but there is no reason to ship an fstab its own checker rejects.

1.reason: New in LFS 13.1 (2026-09-07 bump): an /boot/efi vfat fstab line for a UEFI system. This host boots GRUB BIOS/MBR on sdb with no separate EFI System Partition (host.toml's [hardware].boot), so there is nothing at /dev/<zzz> for this line to name. True of this machine's disk layout, not of LFS in general -- a UEFI host would want it, hence the drop lives here rather than in the shared file.

cat > /etc/lsb-release << "EOF"
DISTRIB_ID="Linux From Scratch"
DISTRIB_RELEASE="13.1-systemd"
DISTRIB_CODENAME="claude-managed"

1.reason: Shared blocks 1-2 only fill the book's `<your name here>` placeholder, but an override stores the whole command, so they also froze the version the book printed when recorded: 13.0. book/13.1 prints 13.1-systemd and this host pins lfs=13.1. Cannot be fixed in the shared file -- laptop is still on 13.0 and reads the same entry. Placeholder value unchanged. Caught because the built tree had /etc/lfs-release (block 0, not overridden) at 13.1 next to these two at 13.0; --check cannot see it, since the override is applied exactly as written and it is the writing that is stale.

10.cmd:
usermod -p '*' root
echo "### root has no password -- reachable only through sudo (wheel)"
10.reason: Requested 2026-09-22: remove the root password altogether. The shared decision sets the placeholder 'lfs-changeme' because the book's `passwd root` (chapter08/shadow.html, 8.30.3) is interactive; that placeholder is a working password. This host gets john with wheel/NOPASSWD sudo (adduser-john, blfs-sudo), so root never needs one. `usermod -p '*'` replaces the hash with '*', which no crypt() output can match: login, su and ssh password auth for root all fail, and unlike laptop's `passwd -l` no hash survives behind a '!' for `passwd -u` to restore. Not `passwd -d`: an empty field lets login accept root with no password. Consequence: systemd's rescue/emergency targets run sulogin, which refuses a locked root unless SYSTEMD_SULOGIN_FORCE=1 is on the kernel command line (systemd-sulogin-shell then passes --force); init=/bin/bash also works.
